Meantime, mechanical properties are important for designing thermoelectric devices.

articleTitle: The spatial anisotropy of the wire metamaterials in the millimeter waveband
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: The paper is devoted to the experimental study of the spectral characteristics of matrix anisotropic structures formed by different type of metamaterial. During the analysis of the spectrum of the structures under investigation the manifestation of spatial anisotropy for different orientations of the wave vector k in the structure has been discovered. This phenomenon is explained by changes of the geometric parameters of metallic inclusions in these structures. Thus increasing the length of the metal inclusions leads to an increase of spatial anisotropy for the both selected different orientations of the wave vector k.

articleTitle: Coupled plasmon hybrid modes in aggregates of metal nanowires
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: Investigation of the plasmonic resonances in aggregates of metal nanowires is presented. Mechanism of plasmonic mode coupling in a system of metal wires that can be considered as hybridization combinations of isolated wire plasmons is investigated.

articleTitle: Two-dimensional periodic structures: Investigation, application and methods for solving problems of diffraction of electromagnetic waves
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: Periodic structures are widely used in different areas of science and technology, forming the grounds for various types of devices [1]. In the microwave range diffraction gratings are used as polarizers, frequency-selective surfaces, quasi-optical beam splitters, protective masking materials that are transparent to electromagnetic waves. Periodic structures are slow-wave structures in electronic devices and in accelerators. An optical grating is the main element of spectrometers.

articleTitle: Control of the planar photonic crystal loaded by varactor diodes spectrum
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: The electrical tuning of the planar photonic crystal, with elements, loaded by varactor diodes, is demonstrated experimentally. It is shown that by increasing the bias voltage the central frequency of the band gap growth monotonically.

articleTitle: Creation and investigation of active nanocomposites based on synthetic opals
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: The work is devoted to the experimental study of the synthetic opals optical properties and matrix nanocomposites based on them with consideration of structural defects. Analysis of Raman spectra and X-Ray diffraction of nanocomposite opal-Bi<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">12</sub>SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">20</sub> has shown that crystallization process of Bismuth silicon oxide could lead to the appearance of γ-phase. The enhancement of intensity of Raman and fluorescence spectra was observed. We have established that increase of structural defects amount in opal results in an increase of emission intensity of nanocomposites.

articleTitle: A model for conductivity and permittivity of heterogeneous systems with complex microstructures
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: The studies of the effective bulk properties of various heterogeneous systems, such as dispersions, composite electrolytes, nanocomposites, and nanofluids (suspensions of nanoparticles), have attracted and keep attracting considerable interest. The reason is that these systems can demonstrate unusual properties which are not typical of pure materials. In particularly, their effective conductivity and permittivity can reveal drastic percolation-type growth, non-monotonous behavior, etc. The existing quantitative theories of these are often far from being satisfactory. The elaboration of pertinent consistent models inevitably leads one to the necessity of working out in detail the microstructure of the system and attacking essentially many-particle problems.

articleTitle: The field structure of open resonant system with multifocal mirror
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: The obtaining of sufficient interaction length in diffraction radiation oscillators (DRO), that are working on THz-frequencies, is the actual problem of diffraction electronics. The one of the ways to resolve this problem is the use of composed focused mirror in the open resonant system (ORS). The work goal is the experimental investigations of the resonant modes properties in ORS with focused mirror, composed from several cylindrical reflectors, having the same radius of curvature. For H-polarization of modes it is obtained the field distributions and Q-factor on frequencies 25-38 GHz, if focused mirror was composed from 2, 3 and 4 cylindrical reflectors. The use of the focused mirror, composed form 2 reflectors, is more attractive for DRO worked on TEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">00q</sub>-resonant mode. When focused mirror is composed from 2, 3 and 4 cylindrical reflectors, the best properties are obtained for TEM<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">(n-1)0q</sub>-modes, that having the null of resonant field near the attachment of reflectors.

articleTitle: Generalized reciprocity relations for resonant diffraction at metal gratings
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: Diffraction theory of electromagnetic waves is of significant value in modern optics and engineering [1,2]. One of its classical chapters constitute problems of light scattering from periodic structures, among which reflecting metal gratings are of particular interest. Diffraction at such gratings can lead to resonant excitation of surface electromagnetic waves (SEWs), which in optics are commonly called surface plasmon-polaritons [2,3]. Investigation of corresponding problems is very intensive in last decades, that is related to interesting characteristics of SEW field (high intensity and localization) useful for various applications [3]. For instance, excitation of SEWs can be used for polarization control of specularly reflected wave, significant enhancement of light absorption by a highly reflective media, suppression of specular reflection and realization of predicted energy flux distribution between different nonspecular outgoing diffracted waves.

articleTitle: Super-resolution microscopy
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: Conventional optical microscopy is limited by diffraction barrier, so for long time improving of resolution was considered impossible. Recent development in super-resolution imaging increases possibilities in researches of different fields such as medicine, biology, material science etc.

articleTitle: Heat convection of viscous incompressible liquid in a cylindrical elementary convection cell with a conical cavity bottom and solid boundary conditions
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: There was studied the task of heat convection of viscous incompressible liquid in a cylindrical elementary convection cell with a conical cavity bottom and solid boundary conditions. Stokes' functions were constructed for cylindrical convection cell as well as for the conical cavity in the cell bottom. Basing on Fujiwhara effect there were obtained Stokes streamline and disturbed temperature model distributions in the cylindrical elementary convection cell with conical cavity bottom and solid boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Search and study of planetary lightning with UTR-2 radio telescope
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: Planetary lightning is a wide spread phenomenon in the Solar system. For today, we know at least 4 planets with stormy atmospheres: Earth, Saturn, Jupiter and Uranus. The largest radio telescope in decameter range UTR-2 has been observing Saturn lightning since 2006. Due to the simultaneous observation with the spacecraft Cassini the reliability of the ground-based observation data was proved. To date we provide numerous observations of Saturn, Uranus and Venus electromagnetic radiation and therefore we are caring out the multistage data processing.

articleTitle: Verification of left-handed behavior of mode with circular polarization for chiral multilayered structure
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: Thus, the experimental and numerical studies of electromagnetic properties of layered chiral media in the millimeter waveband are carried out. It is shown that the chiral structure based on rosettes massive exhibits the left-handed properties for one of the circularly polarized waves. This is manifested the negative frequency dispersion of the structure under study. The authors thank V.P. Ruban (IRE NASU) for help in preparing the research samples.

articleTitle: On the theory of a circular waveguide with anisotropic impedance surface for gyro-devices: Eigenmodes
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: Circular waveguides with anisotropic impedance surfaces can be used in gyro-devices in order to improve their performance. Among them are dielectric-loaded metallic waveguides [1–5], axially [6] and azimuthally [7] corrugated waveguides. Their eigenmodes are purely (or nearly) TE and TM modes only in a number of extreme cases. Such cases were considered previously in [1–7]. However, in the general case, when the surface impedance is arbitrary, waveguide modes are hybrid HE and EH waves. Derivation of the boundary-value problem for such waves is the main aim of the study.

articleTitle: Fine structure of the pulsar decameter radiation as the probe of the propagation media
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: Pulsars radiate short pulsed signals (a typical period of an ordinary pulsar is about 1 s) that are good probes of propagation media. Propagation medium includes pulsar magnetosphere, interstellar medium (ISM), interplanetary medium (IPM) and the Earth's ionosphere, it has turbulent nature with variation of the electron density along the line-of-sight. During pulses propagation they are influenced by free electrons, irregularities of the electron concentration and magnetic field. It causes the propagation effects that are called frequency dispersion delay, scattering and the Faraday rotation respectively. At low frequencies all the propagation effects are most contrasted and this imposes restrictions on the pulsar observations in this frequency range. In fact, we are able to investigate only the nearest to the Earth pulsars with low dispersion measures (DM, describes amount of free electrons on the line of sight). Fortunately, at low frequency about 1 – 2 % of all pulsar pulses are ten or hundred times more intensive than average pulses. This phenomenon is called the pulsar anomalously intense pulses (AIP) [1] and gives opportunities to study fine structures of pulsar individual pulses at these frequencies. Fine structure of the pulsar radiation is short pulses inside the main pulse, it was detected by Hankins [2]. Characteristic time scale of the fine structure is frequency dependent, at decameters it is the widest, in the paper [3] authors detected the fine structure of pulsar B0809+74 with time-scale 2 – 4 ms, using radio telescope UTR-2.

articleTitle: Decameter pulsar/transient survey of northern sky. Multiparametric pipeline candidate selection
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: Radio telescope UTR-2 has recently accomplished a survey of the northern sky to find pulsars and transient sources of radio emission. On the one hand, studies in such a low-frequency range are very difficult because of the extremely high influence of scattering in the interstellar medium, very strong radio interference and high temperature of Galactic background. On the other hand, large dispersion delay allows to determine the dispersion measure (DM) of broadband signals with a small characteristic length very accurately.

articleTitle: Estimation of Z′ boson parameters by the forward-backward asymmetry of Drell-Yan process at 7 TeV at the LHC
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: The forward-backward asymmetry of the Drell-Yan process at the LHC at 7 TeV is investigated. It is found that in some kinematical areas the 1“2σ deviations of the CMS results from the Standard model predictions are observed. These deviations are treated in terms of Z' boson. In the model-independent approach, the Z' vector and axial-vector couplings to the Standard model fermions are estimated at the mass m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z'</sub> = 3 TeV and 3,5 TeV and Γ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z'</sub> / m<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Z'</sub> = 0,1. It is shown that at 1σ level Z' boson signal can be clearly distinguished from the CMS data. It is observed also that this result does not depend strongly on the Z' mass.

articleTitle: Thermal vacuum processing of brown coal
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: Thermal vacuum processing method of brown coal is presented. The proposed method allows to obtain a fine powder of brown coal with a moisture content of 0.8% and up to 40 nm in a continuous drying and reducing it in the content of sulfur and nitrogen, which reduces harmful emissions into the atmosphere during its combustion to power station. Principle of the developed energy efficiency thermal vacuum drying apparatus is described. On the basis of experimental studies of the rate of two-phase flow is obtained, providing performance of the apparatus. The process of removing moisture from the brown coal during thermal vacuum drying unit is simulated, the results of the research are presented.

articleTitle: Ground states of magnetic spherical shells
publicationTitle: 2015 International Young Scientists Forum on Applied Physics (YSF)
abstract: A competition between short-range exchange and long-range magnetostatic interactions results in nontrivial distribution of magnetization in a magnetic nanoparticle [1]. Such magnetic distributions as vortex and onion are widely studied for the case of planar structures. Recently a significant interest to nanomagnets with curved shape appears. On the one hand it is due to modern techniques of fabrication of nanoparticles of a custom shape, and on the other hand the curvature might significantly change magnetic properties of the sample and cause new effects [2].
